_contract.why: Hand-authored from CONTRACT.md v1.0 before CallCenterWeb/* exists. Shape is contract; values are illustrative. Replaced by a real capture at first integration (CONTRACT.md §11).
_contract.scenario: The two concurrency shapes: a routine strict-claim collision the client rides out, and the requestId replay that makes an ambiguous retry safe. Plus the stale-tab refusal.

response.message: Another request is updating this order.

replay._note: Same requestId as `busy`, resent after the claim freed. It applied on an earlier attempt whose response was lost; the ledger recognises it.

data._elided: current state — NOT the state as of the original apply

staleTab._note: The agent abandoned this order and opened a fresh one for a new caller; a forgotten tab fires an add on the dead id.

response.message: This order was cancelled and can no longer be changed.

secondOpen._note: One active order per agent — the refusal that IS the reconnect story (127).

_notes: SESSION_BUSY is ROUTINE, not an outage: the 15 s strict claim is the only mutual exclusion in the engine (SaveAsync blind-increments Version — 127 finding 1). The client retries 0·400·800·1600·3200 ms in features/callcenter/api.ts, never in core/api.ts.

The explicit, ownership-validated transactionId is what makes staleTab a refusal instead of caller A's item landing on caller B's live order — the same harm 127 refused auto-resume to prevent, closed on the other side.
refusedExisting rides the SUCCESS path: it is a choice (resume or abandon-and-open-fresh), not a failure. Never a silent auto-resume.
